sourceAttempts.result: Describes the San Juan from Navajo Dam to Blanco as a relaxing 17-mile float runnable any time of year and notes diversion dams downstream toward Shiprock.

Provides exact public access coordinates and river-mile sequence for Navajo Dam, Blanco, Vereda del Rio and Among the Waters Park; documents Class I–II character, year-round planning, diversion dams and hidden fences.
Provides statewide PFD, weather and float-plan guidance and warns that low-head dams and strainers can be deadly; San Juan is specifically included among rivers with low-head dams.
USGS 09355500 near Archuleta and 09365000 at Farmington provide direct discharge and stage telemetry for the selected upper and lower reaches.
Added a San Juan-specific U.S. Bureau of Reclamation Navajo Dam photograph instead of reusing the Rio Grande image.

The published Navajo Dam, Blanco, Vereda del Rio and Among the Waters sequence supports three additional distinct day or staged multi-day combinations while retaining named intermediate bailouts and the appropriate upper/lower direct gauges.
